skill.name: runcomfy-cli
skill.description: Use the RunComfy CLI to submit hosted image and video jobs, check their status, and download the results. The skill covers sign-in, model input schemas, and scripting with JSON output.
skill.summary: Run hosted image and video jobs from the terminal and track their results.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match Markdown formatting, links, or routine RunComfy account checks. The skill documents ordinary hosted model use, but unpinned installs, shell argument handling, remote input submission, and retries after timeouts carry risks. No evidence found of deliberate credential exfiltration or an attempt to override audit instructions.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the skill to a reviewed commit and the CLI to an exact release. Verify provenance and integrity, and require approval before installing globally.
Distinguish CLI parsing from shell parsing. Pass structured arguments or use a securely created input file rather than interpolating prompt text into a shell command.

remediation.issue: Remote submission without an explicit data approval step
remediation.suggestion: Show which prompts, files, and URLs will be sent to RunComfy. Require user approval before submitting sensitive data or selected local files.
Check the original request status before resubmitting. When acceptance is unknown, use documented idempotency support or ask the user before submitting a new job.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned installation sources
semantic_findings.description: The setup examples install a skill from a repository and fetch a CLI package without fixing either revision. The package commands can execute releases different from those reviewed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples name a repository and package without an immutable reference or exact version. There is no evidence that either source is compromised.

semantic_findings.title: Shell safety guarantee omits caller-side quoting
semantic_findings.description: The skill claims there is no shell injection surface from prompts. A shell can still interpret prompt text if the caller builds an inline command without protecting the argument.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The claim concerns CLI parsing, but shell parsing happens first. The quoted batch example treats prompt text as data, so no unsafe interpolation is shown there.

semantic_findings.title: Local request data can leave the workspace
semantic_findings.description: The CLI can read a local request file and send its body to RunComfy. The skill does not require reviewing the file contents before transmission.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The input-file option and HTTPS submission are explicitly documented. The risk is unintended disclosure through legitimate use, not evidence of covert exfiltration.

semantic_findings.title: Timeout retries may create duplicate paid jobs
semantic_findings.description: The retry loop submits another job after exit code 75, which includes polling timeouts. If the original job was accepted, resubmission may incur another charge.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The loop reruns submission without checking the original request. The document does not establish whether the service deduplicates submissions or cancels timed-out jobs.

content.user_title: Run Image and Video Models with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Hosted media models use different input fields and job settings. The RunComfy CLI skill helps you find the right schema, submit a request, and track the result from the terminal.
actual_capabilities: Set up browser sign-in or use an environment token for unattended sessions.
Find endpoint input schemas in the API tab on RunComfy model pages.
Submit image and video jobs with inline JSON or a JSON or YAML input file.
Wait for results or return a request ID and check its status later.
Choose a local output directory or return results without downloading files.
Use JSON output to extract request IDs or result URLs in scripts.
limitations: Model processing runs on RunComfy and requires network access and an authenticated account.
The CLI must be installed separately. The skill does not include the CLI binary or model files.
Required input fields vary by endpoint. Check the model's API tab before submitting.
A local timeout does not establish that a remote job stopped. Check its status before submitting again.

use_cases.title: Generate a concept image
use_cases.description: Choose a text-to-image model, submit a non-sensitive concept prompt, and download the result to a project folder.

use_cases.title: Track a long video job
use_cases.description: Submit a video job without waiting, keep the request ID, and check the result when it is ready.

use_cases.title: Plan an image generation batch
use_cases.description: Review a list of prompts and prepare a batch that records request IDs and output locations for each job.

prompt_templates.title: Check my RunComfy setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether the RunComfy CLI is installed and signed in. Report the version and sign-in status without displaying or requesting my token.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a concept image request
prompt_templates.scenario: Novice: Run a first text-to-image job.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the required inputs for the RunComfy text-to-image model I select. Show me the prompt and output directory before submitting one job.

prompt_templates.title: Submit a video job for later review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Track an asynchronous video request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the approved video request against its model schema. Submit it without waiting, return the request ID, and check that same job when I ask.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a bounded image batch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Prepare a batch before starting remote work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my prompt file and plan up to five image requests. Use JSON output to track each job. Ask before submitting, and do not retry ambiguous timeouts automatically.

output_examples.input: Generate one concept image from my approved product sketch prompt and put it in the concepts folder.
output_examples.output: The image job completed and one result was downloaded to the concepts folder.

output_examples.input: Submit my approved video job without waiting. Do not download the result yet.
output_examples.output: The video job was submitted and a request ID was returned. No files were downloaded. Use that ID to check the same job later.

output_examples.input: Check why my image request failed.
output_examples.output: The model rejected the request because a required input field was missing. Check the endpoint schema before submitting again.

best_practices: Check the exact endpoint schema and confirm the request contents before sending data to RunComfy.
Pass prompt text as structured data instead of inserting it directly into shell commands.
Keep request IDs and check their status before retrying a request that timed out.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API tokens into prompts or commit them to a repository.
Do not install unreviewed packages or pipe remote installers into a shell.
Do not submit confidential files or unrelated reference URLs without approval.

faq.question: Does this skill run models locally?
faq.answer: No. The CLI sends requests to RunComfy for processing. Downloaded results can be kept locally.

faq.question: How do I sign in?
faq.answer: Use the CLI browser sign-in for interactive work. In CI, provide the RunComfy token through your secret manager.

faq.question: Where do I find the model's input schema?
faq.answer: Open the model's detail page in the RunComfy catalog and select the API tab.

faq.question: Can I submit a job and check it later?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the no-wait option to get a request ID, then check that ID with the status command.

faq.question: Can I keep a result URL without downloading a file?
faq.answer: Yes. Skip downloads and use JSON output to read result URLs once the job completes.

faq.question: Should I resubmit a job after a timeout?
faq.answer: Check the original request first. A timeout can end local polling while the remote job is still running.
